page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 48 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB per core allocation. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, but it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, with read-only large block speeds reaching 435.08 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 256.67 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 81868.98 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 24039.0. The instance also exhibits top-tier results in software compilation and database operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1706.59, and text generation for small LLM models is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the poor category at 30.43 tokens/sec.

The ARM-based architecture provides high resource density and memory bandwidth efficiency, making it a cost-effective option for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 architectures. Given its high network bandwidth and strong multi-core capabilities, this instance is suited for static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.12xlarge is an ARM64 general-purpose instance powered by 48 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. It features 192.0 GB of memory, a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps, and no local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results indicate top-tier memory bandwidth, with uncached read speeds of 435.08 GB/sec, and strong multi-core processing, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 24039.0. The instance excels in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving, though single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation are relatively weaker. This profile makes it highly efficient for multi-threaded, network-intensive workloads.
